---
description: Read a past session from any AI agent and bring it into this conversation
argument-hint: "[session id, or words from its title] [--tools] [--mode brief|custom|full] [--cap N] [--thinking] [--start N --end N] [--no-summarize]"
allowed-tools: Bash(ectype:*)
---
<!-- generated by ectype skill install: command /ectype -->

Bring a past session into this conversation with `ectype recall`. `$ARGUMENTS` is empty, a
session id (any prefix), or words to search for, optionally followed by options that
`ectype recall` understands. Options typed here win over the defaults in ectype's Settings →
Agent skill.

1. **Find it.** With no argument, run `ectype list -n 20`, show the table, and ask which one.
   With words, run `ectype search '<words>'` first (one quoted pattern): it first summarises the sessions that are
   new or changed since the last search, then greps every summary ectype keeps, and says how many
   sessions it covered. If nothing matches, run `ectype list -n 60`
   and pick the row whose id starts with the argument or whose title contains it. If several
   match, show only those and ask; never guess between two.

2. **Bring it in at the right depth.** Run `ectype recall <id>` with the options the user typed.
   The defaults come from Settings → Agent skill, which start at the conversation alone: the
   user's and the agent's messages, a question the agent put to the user with the answer, and
   any message another session sent in (under `[PEER]`), with no tool calls. On a 989-message
   session that is about 11 K tokens instead of 348 K. If that does not answer the question,
   re-read the part that does rather than the whole session:
   - `--tools` adds every tool call by name; `--tools --mode custom --cap 300` adds the first
     300 tokens of each result too;
   - `--thinking` adds the reasoning, which is large;
   - `--start 40 --end 80` is a message range.

   With `--tools`, the tool-output mode is `--mode brief` (names only, the default), `--mode
   custom` (results capped at `--cap`) or `--mode full` (everything); a word the user typed such
   as `--brief` or `--full` means `--tools` with the matching `--mode`. `ectype recall --help`
   lists every option.

3. **It is remembered.** Unless `--no-summarize` was given (or Settings says otherwise), recall
   also saves the session's summary into ectype's own store, which is what `ectype search` reads
   next time. Say so in one line when it happens; the command prints the path on stderr.

4. **Say what you took.** End by telling the user which session, which view, and roughly what
   it cost, so the context they are now paying for is visible rather than implied.

Do not run `ectype convert` or install anything unless the user asks in so many words: those
write into an agent's own store.
